retainedRun.scope: Disposable local PostgreSQL repository/worker with deterministic source/provider stubs, eight recovery scenarios, a four-worker 100-row drain, append-only evidence/notification reconciliation, and a corrected concurrent five-second compiled query-service mix.

retainedAlarmRun.scope: All 18 required synthetic warning/stop alarms delivered ALARM and recovery OK through one exact ephemeral SNS topic to an encrypted SQS receiver; all 36 messages were acknowledged with no duplicates and every ephemeral resource was verified absent after cleanup.

retainedRollbackRun.scope: Disposable local PostgreSQL plus the shipped ProgramElementReadService and PeSnapshotGateService: populated tenant-canary pointer route, emergency legacy process switch, real authorized pointer rollback from a deliberately defective total of 999 to the exact prior total of 250 and quantity of 12, immutable row-hash preservation, drain pause, outbox suppression, and durable audit assertions.

retainedProductQueryRun.scope: A 1,800-second request-start window against compiled BudgetLifecycleQueryService and PrismaBudgetLifecycleReadStore with a small synthetic Session 12 corpus in disposable local PostgreSQL: 7,108 samples, zero errors, p95 7.599 ms, and 99.98% request-start window coverage. It bypassed HTTP, authentication, network hops, AWS topology, production data, buyer traffic, concurrent outbox drain, and update-latency measurement.

retainedAwsCostObservation.scope: A read-only Cost Explorer observation of nine account-wide AWS services over the 30-day window ending 2026-09-25. The simple annualized account-wide run rate is numerically below the Package 9 cap, but no defense-budget or Package 9 cost-allocation boundary is present, so the incremental cost gate remains unqualified.

invariants: Every accepted fact has a durable immutable evidence identity before it is acknowledged.
After recovery, every accepted fact is present exactly once by logical identity; retries may create attempt records but never a second logical fact.
A logical notification key is emitted at most once, including across crash, lease expiry, retry, and replay.
Provider or source outage never converts missing evidence into acceptance, a negative assertion, or a fabricated fact.
Rollback stops admission and consumers or returns readers to the prior pointer without deleting or mutating immutable evidence.

workload.identityRule: Generate stable sourceFactId and logicalNotificationKey from seed and ordinal 0001-0100; preserve the mapping in the run manifest.
workload.providerLane: deterministic local stub; paid budget remains zero
workload.duration: Run steady drain for 30 minutes or until all accepted work is reconciled; separately age one held item to the 60-minute alarm threshold using a controllable test clock.
workload.measurement: Capture queue depth and age each minute; task concurrency and runtime; accepted/evidence/acknowledged/recovered identity sets; notification keys; common-query p50/p95/max; retries and DLQ; AWS and provider cost deltas.

scenarios.failure: Terminate the worker after immutable evidence commit and before outbox acknowledgement.
procedure: Seed the baseline workload in an isolated disposable environment.
Pause at the evidence-commit/ack boundary and terminate exactly one worker for sourceFactId ordinal 0001.
Restart with the same image/config and drain within the limits; query by stable fact and notification keys.
passAssertions: 100/100 accepted sourceFactIds have one committed evidence identity.
The interrupted item is safely recognized on replay; no accepted fact is omitted.
Each logical notification key has at most one delivered logical notification.
Pending rows never exceed 100; DLQ never exceeds 10; drain concurrency <=4.
coOwners: named source owner in run manifest

scenarios.failure: Hold a leased job beyond its configured expiry, then let a second worker reclaim it while the original worker is prevented from acknowledging stale ownership.
procedure: Use a controllable clock and two workers against one isolated queue item.
Expire the first lease, reclaim with worker two, then release the stale worker.
Reconcile attempts, evidence identities, queue state, and notification keys.
passAssertions: Exactly one current lease owner can acknowledge the item.
The stale owner cannot delete, overwrite, or acknowledge the newer lease.
The accepted fact is retained once logically and notification key emitted at most once.
Retry count and lease transitions are auditable; queue and task limits hold.
coOwners: named source owner in run manifest

scenarios.failure: Inject a transient failure on the first attempt, then restore the dependency for the bounded retry.
procedure: Apply the fault to deterministic ordinals 0021-0030 only.
Allow only the configured bounded retry policy; record each attempt and idempotency key.
Drain the remaining baseline workload and compare accepted/evidence/notification sets.
passAssertions: All accepted items converge without exceeding maxAttemptsPerDecision=2 where model decision attempts apply.
Retry does not duplicate logical evidence or notifications.
No item is silently dropped or reclassified as accepted without evidence.
DLQ remains <=10 and provides exact recoverable identities if a bounded retry is exhausted.
coOwners: named source owner in run manifest
model/evaluation lead when provider decision is involved

scenarios.failure: Make one named source unavailable for a fixed interval while other source families remain available.
procedure: Use a source-specific adapter stub for deterministic ordinals 0041-0060.
Return timeout/5xx for 10 minutes, then restore source access without moving its watermark past unobserved records.
Continue unrelated source families and replay the exact source interval.
passAssertions: Unavailable source is marked delayed/unknown, never complete or empty.
No watermark skips the outage interval; recovered interval is reconciled from exact cursor overlap.
No accepted facts are lost and no logical notifications duplicate after recovery.
Oldest pending age alarm fires by 60 minutes; interactive query p95 remains <=2,000 ms.
scenarios.primaryOwner: named source owner in run manifest

scenarios.failure: Return timeout, 429, malformed response, and 5xx from the provider boundary in separate deterministic sub-runs.
procedure: Use only a local provider stub; paid provider allocation stays $0.
Pin model identifier and request/response fixture hashes in each sub-run.
Exercise timeout, throttling, malformed result, and recovery; reconcile decisions and cost ledger.
passAssertions: Provider failure yields bounded retry or abstention/review, never a fabricated accepted fact.
Source evidence envelope survives every failed attempt.
Provider retries are capped and accounted; paid invocation count and spend remain zero.
No duplicate logical notification; queue/DLQ and query budgets hold.

scenarios.failure: Sustain the 100-item baseline while four drain tasks run and common reads execute concurrently.
procedure: Load the stable seeded workload to a peak of 100 pending rows.
Run no more than four drain tasks for at most 30 minutes each.
Issue the versioned common-query mix continuously and record raw latency samples.
passAssertions: Pending <=100, DLQ <=10, oldest age <=60 minutes, drain tasks <=4.
Common interactive query p95 <=2,000 ms.
Verified program update p95 <=60 minutes.
Measured annualized AWS projection is <=$1,000 with assumptions disclosed; provider paid spend is $0 in this lane.
executedAssertions: The local synthetic product reader sustained a 1,800-second request-start window across four closed-loop clients and all eight declared operations: 7,108 samples, zero errors, 1,799.657 seconds first-to-last request-start span, and a final start 342.839 milliseconds before the deadline.

Direct compiled service/read-store latency was p50 4.032 milliseconds, p95 7.599 milliseconds, and maximum 248.564 milliseconds, below the 2,000-millisecond limit in this limited local synthetic environment.
The benchmark login was NOINHERIT with no memberships and zero effective table-write privileges across 494 public tables.

The corrected concurrent run held a 100-row peak, used four drain workers, finished at pending/leased/dead-letter 0/0/0, and reconciled 100 evidence identities plus 100 logical notifications with no missing or duplicate keys.

During that drain, four clients issued 20 error-free requests covering all eight declared compiled service/read-store operations; p95 was 153.05 milliseconds and monotonic overlap was 4,064.7537 milliseconds.
All eight crash, lease, retry, source, and local provider-fault scenarios passed, and all four workload source families reconciled at 25 rows each.

A read-only 30-day Cost Explorer observation found $6.1100983972 across nine relevant account-wide service totals and a simple $74.33953049926667 annualized account-wide run rate. This is supporting context only because the account has no Package 9-specific cost-allocation boundary.
unqualifiedAssertions: The concurrent query window was only five seconds; the separate 30-minute query run was not concurrent with the drain, so sustained production-representative concurrency remains unqualified.
Both query runs bypassed HTTP, authentication, browser and network latency, used a small synthetic corpus, and were not production or buyer traffic.
Verified source-change-to-buyer-visible update p95 was not measured, and the AWS observation cannot attribute account-wide cost to Package 9 incremental spend.
This limited component evidence does not make the full P9-L01 scenario PASS or authorize activation.

scenarios.failure: Inject a post-canary defect and roll routing plus the active read projection back to the last qualified revision.
procedure: Record the current qualified routing and projection pointers plus immutable evidence counts.
Activate one isolated canary scope, inject the defect, stop admission, and execute the documented rollback.
Reconcile pointers, immutable evidence, audit events, queue identities, and client-visible reads.
passAssertions: Routing and active projection return to the exact prior qualified revisions within the declared recovery target.
Immutable evidence, source bytes, attempts, manifests, review decisions, and notification ledgers are unchanged except for append-only rollback events.
No unqualified canary fact remains current and no accepted historical fact is lost.
executedAssertions: The shipped ProgramElementReadService and PeSnapshotGateService routed a synthetic tenant canary through a populated active snapshot and exposed its deliberately defective FY2027 total of 999; the emergency process switch returned the explicit legacy sentinel without snapshot row reads.

The real promotion engine executed an authorized rollback to the populated prior snapshot; the post-rollback canary returned the exact prior FY2027 total of 250 and quantity of 12 through ProgramElementReadService.
Both snapshots, every immutable candidate row hash, the prior Program Element identity and positions, and append-only activation and rollback audit records remained present and unchanged.
Rollback wrote a side-effect drain pause; a paused drain claimed no rows; rollback produced no unsuppressed alert-eligible output.
The general serve role could not move the pointer or mutate canonical rows, and active-snapshot reads did not mix snapshots.
unqualifiedAssertions: The populated responses used synthetic local rows; no production-size, customer-owned, or independently adjudicated response-equivalence corpus participated.
No authenticated HTTP request, restarted deployed API, production database, real source byte, or delivered customer notification participated.
This limited local composite pass does not authorize production or paid activation.

scenarios.failure: Cross each warning and stop threshold in an isolated run and verify delivery to the named receiver without affecting production workloads.
procedure: Bind named alarm receivers and record exact alarm/rule identities before injection.
Cross queue depth, DLQ, age, task-count, runtime, latency, AWS-cost and provider-cost thresholds one at a time with test metrics.
Record alarm state transition, receiver acknowledgement, stop-admission action and recovery.
passAssertions: Every required alarm transitions and reaches its named receiver within the declared delivery window.
Each stop threshold prevents new admission while preserving queued and immutable evidence.
Missing, delayed, misrouted, or unacknowledged alarm delivery fails qualification.
executedAssertions: All 18 required warning and stop alarms established an initial OK baseline with actions disabled; two consecutive 20-second receiver polls were empty before actions were enabled.

Each threshold was crossed sequentially and delivered an identity-matched ALARM notification, then recovered and delivered an identity-matched OK notification to the encrypted exact-source SQS receiver.
All 36 notifications were acknowledged within 4.586 to 16.652 seconds against the explicitly harness-only 600-second limit, with zero duplicate deliveries.
Every alarm history contained both ALARM and OK transitions; all 18 alarms, the subscription, topic, queue, and local temporary files were deleted and verified absent.
unqualifiedAssertions: No named human or production receiver participated.
Stop-admission and queued or immutable evidence preservation were not exercised.
The full P9-F07 scenario therefore is not PASS and cannot authorize activation.
coOwners: named source owner in run manifest
